mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thereby driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not positively correlated with low FEDFUNDS levels in more than 40% of the cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate suggests a weak labor market, which could lead to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns when UNRATE exceeds 7.5% in more than 30% of cases, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive economic growth and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high real savings rate suggests consumers are saving more and spending less, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS exceeds 400,000 but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 25% of cases, the hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment is high but payroll employment is increasing, it may indicate a mixed labor market signal, leading to uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the hypothesis predicts negative returns but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of cases, it is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production suggests strong economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, high federal funds rates may lead to decreased borrowing and investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If during tightening, high FEDFUNDS does not predict negative returns in more than 35% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth coupled with high inflation may lead to uncertainty and potential rate hikes, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the combination of GDPC1 and CPIAUCSL does not predict negative returns in more than 30% of cases, the hypothesis is invalid.
